messages.body_plain:
Here is a mod that adds a plot to Evaluate to show predicted values
against observed with a pseudo-R-square.  The code seems to work well,
but does NOT include provision to also output to the log.

File: rattle.R  (function: getSelectedVariables)
    ## And finally, remove the na.omit if there is one, replacing it
    ## with specifically removing just the rows that were removed in
    ## the predict command.

    if (not.null(omitted))
      scoreset = sub(")", "[-omitted,]", sub("na.omit\\(", "",
scoreset))
      obsset <- scoreset   #**********Save copy for mod referred to
below************
    scoreset <- sprintf('subset(%s, select=c(%s))',
                        scoreset,
                        ifelse(is.null(idents), "",
                               sprintf('"%s"', paste(idents,
collapse='", "'))))
    appendLog("Extract the corresponding identifier fields from the
dataset.",
             sprintf("scores <- %s", scoreset))

    scores <- eval(parse(text=scoreset))

#Modification by Ed Cox to plot predictions vs. observed values
    obsset <- sprintf('subset(%s, select=crs$target)',obsset)
    obs <- eval(parse(text=obsset))
    fitpoints <- cbind(obs,Predicted=crs$pr)
    fitcorr <- format(cor(fitpoints[,1],fitpoints[,2]),digits=4)
    op <- par(c(lty="solid",col="blue"))
    plot(fitpoints,asp=1,main="Predicted vs.
Observed",sub=paste("Pseudo R-square = ",fitcorr))
    prline <- lm(fitpoints[,2]~fitpoints[,1])
    abline(prline)
    par(c(lty="dashed",col="black"))
    abline(0,1)  #add a diagonal representing perfect correlation.
    legend("topleft",legend=c("Best Fit to Points","Ideal
Regression"),
           lty=c(1,2),col=c("blue","black"),bty="n"  )
    par(op)
#End Mod

    appendLog("Write the scores to file.",
             paste('write.csv(cbind(scores, predict=crs$pr), file="',
                   score.file, '", row.names=FALSE)', sep=""))

    write.csv(cbind(scores, predict=crs$pr), file=score.file,
row.names=FALSE)

    infoDialog("The scores for", mtype, "have been saved into the
file",
               paste(getwd(), score.file, sep="/"))

messages.subject: Repeat load from ODBC fails
messages.body_plain:
I have noticed that when I import data from an ODBC source and then
later try to reload it that it fails.  The error message does not
always appear consistent.  I have had to exit rattle and restart it.
I am using your source code (2.2.216), but I think the last stable
release (84) was also doing it.  Does this ring any bells?

- Ed

messages.subject: Recent updates to Rattle (2.2.92)
messages.body_plain:
It's time for an update on progress with Rattle. Overall details are
available from

  http://rattle.togaware.com/

An updated version will be released through CRAN at some stage, but as
always,
the latest version is available by downloading:

  http://rattle.togaware.com/src/contrib/rattle_2.2.92.tar.gz

and then

  $ R CMD INSTALL rattle_2.2.92.tar.gz

or (for MS/Windows) download:

  http://rattle.togaware.com/src/contrib/rattle_2.2.92.zip

and in R:

  > install.packages("rattle_2.2.92.zip", repos=NULL)

The main updates have been:

Transform:
    Added a new By Group normalisation to the Transform tab (Tony
Nolan)

Data:
    Improved the handling of ID, TARGET variables.

Export:
    Updates from Zementis fopr PMML export (ksvm, logisitc regression)

Evaluate:
    Add a Predicted versus Observed plot (Ed Cox)

213 071220 Resync
212 071220 Update note on quantiles for binning
211 071212 Robust kmeans using multiple runs for clustering.
210 071212 Add subset sizes to Benfords legend.
209 071205 Explore->Distr->Cat: Add mosaic plots (Rohan Baxter)
208 071201 Transform Remap join categoricals for stratification.
207 071201 Benford: Add "digit/+/-" options (Eugene Dubossarsky)
206 071128 Bug fix: MSWindows useFancyQuotes=TRUE fails in textview
(RGtk2)
205 071126 Add binning (Daniele Medri), log, indicators to Transform-
>Remap.
204 071125 Implement Transform->Cleanup to delete variables from the
dataset.
           Export dataset from Data/Select tab. Depend on reshape.
203 071124 Transform->Normalise implemented: scale, normalise, rank.
(Ed Cox)

 around the Transform Tab, providing a
number of common pre-processing options (normalisation, imputation). A
growing description is available from:

  http://datamining.togaware.com/survivor/Transform.html

(or else from the draft PDF of the book under development - see the
footer of the web page).

The use of the "tune" function is also being incorporated to
automatically find the best parameter settings. An experimental use is
available with the decision tree model builder.

As always, contributions of code are most welcome, as are comments and
suggestions.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Edit Source
messages.body_plain:
I ran across a bug and managed a quick fix, but I know it is only a
band-aid that is not a general solution.  In function:
executeEvaluateScore I made the change shown below.  The issue appears
to be that it complains if there are no NAs to remove so I bypass the
omission code.  I know this is not a general fix because I know I ran
into a case where it failed, but maybe you will have the insight as to
what the real problem is and can do it right.

(PS: The project I was working on was very well received and it looks
there is more work coming in the near future!!!  Rattle ROCKS!)

    ## First deal with the na.omit case, to capture the list of rows
    ## omitted.

    #Mod by Ed Cox to fix error when no NAs in test set
    scorevarlist <-
c(getSelectedVariables("ident"),getSelectedVariables("target"),getSelectedVariables("input"),getSelectedVariables("risk"))
    tmpset <- crs$dataset[-crs$sample, scorevarlist]
    if (substr(scoreset, 1, 7) == "na.omit" & !dim(tmpset)
[1]==dim(na.omit(tmpset))[1] )
    {
      omit.cmd <- paste("omitted <- ", scoreset, "@na.action", sep="")
      appendLog("Record rows omitted from predict command.", omit.cmd)
      eval(parse(text=omit.cmd))
    }
    else
      omitted <- NULL

Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) :
  no slot of name "na.action" for this object of class "data.frame"

As an added note, due to this error I was not able to test your
inclusion of my Pr v Ob chart until now, but when I do I don't see any
data points.  Apparently you are imposing fixed limits of 0 to 1 for
the axis ranges which is not necessarily true when doing linear
regression (which is where this chart is useful).

- Ed

messages.subject: Re: Edit Source
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the bug report Ed.

I've added your na.omit code, and seems to work okay for my regression
testing. If you come across the situation where it fails do let me
know. I'm not yet understanding what the problem is.

Rattle is particularly written with binary classification in mind (and
there remains some coding assumptions that rely on this). I've removed
the fixed (0,1) limits on the axes in the Pr v Ob plot though.

Thanks also for the feedback. Glad to see Rattle is useful.

Regards,
Graham
